claim_summary: ARTIST combines curated interleaved traces and hierarchical RL to train an LLM for question-adaptive temporal segment selection and grounded time-series question answering.

claim_evidence.quote: We present adaptive segment selection for time series reasoning. The model iteratively chooses temporal segments to inspect and updates its reasoning based on the retrieved segments.

modules.name: Hierarchical segment-selection reasoning policy
modules.scope_reason: The shared policy is SFT- and RL-trained to produce temporal reasoning and choose workflow actions from selected-segment and reasoner feedback; R2 places parameter updates on the LLM side.

evidence.quote: As shown in Fig. 2b, we use nested rollouts to obtain separate learning signals for the Controller and Reasoner behavior, and combine them into a joint update.
Segment selection is facilitated through a toolcalling mechanism that enables the model to iteratively retrieve temporal segments.

modules.name: Interleaved time-series reasoning traces
modules.scope_reason: The paper constructs structured traces specifically for supervised fine-tuning of the LLM; R2 explicitly places training data built to train the model on the LLM side.

evidence.quote: Supervised fine-tuning reasoning traces follow a structured, interleaved format that alternates between natural-language reasoning and explicit time-series segment selection.

modules.name: Iterative temporal-segment acquisition
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the controller accepts a reasoner's answer as final only when it judges the question-answering evidence sufficient; if the task changed to forecasting, the answer acceptance criterion and interaction state would need redesign. R3_2_GTS is a counterfactual because although the selected data are temporal segments, the procedure is bound to the QA objective rather than task-independent temporal data management.
